name: The Salvation Army
summary: A church that runs the largest network of social services in the United States: food, shelters, help with bills, holiday gifts, disaster relief, residential addiction recovery funded by its thrift stores, and community centres. About 2% of its programme spending supports the international Salvation Army's work abroad.

programs.label: Social services, shelter, recovery and community programmes in the US
programs.weight_source: https://dam.redshieldtoolkit.org/asset/3f64b200-2662-4124-b458-e21cb70e49cc/2026-National-Annual-Report.pdf (fiscal 2025, p. 23): programme services $3,546,330k, less the thrift stores' running costs ($739,591k rehabilitation × (1 − 0.25), facts/salvation_army.json rehab_treatment_share, best guess) = $554,693k, less day-care fees ($167,075k × 0.3, day_care_fee_share) = $50,123k, less the overseas work below ($69,696k) = $2,871,818k: the model's program_spend at the best guesses. The overseas work ($69,696k: the World Service Office's programmes and the US territories' contributions to the International Trust) has a draft charityevals model, not yet published (its last audit left the question whether one model may hold several families' branches for the owner), so it has no programme entry yet.
